# 4D Web Action Handler Guardrails

## Scope

This is guidance for methods that process web requests, including methods named with `wa` prefixes and related routing handlers.

## Required Handler Pattern
1. Always begin with authorization branching.
2. Always branch behavior by HTTP method.
3. Always enforce CSRF validation for POST requests.
4. Always use explicit page render or redirect methods.
5. Always wrap handler body with profiling calls.


## Minimum Structure
```4d
//%attributes = {"invisible":true,"shared":true,"preemptive":"capable"}
// ----------------------------------------------------
//             GET/POST ROUTER CALLBACK METHOD
// ----------------------------------------------------
// {METHOD_NAME} (url; hasAuthorized; httpRequestMethod)
// 
// DESCRIPTION
//   Handles "{URL}" urls.
//
#DECLARE($url : Text; $hasAuthorized : Boolean; $httpRequestMethod : Text)
// ----------------------------------------------------

Profiler_START(Current method name)

Case of
: (Not($hasAuthorized))
    WebCore_BadLogin($url)
    
: ($httpRequestMethod="GET")
    // render page

: ($httpRequestMethod="POST")
    // validate CSRF and process post

Else
    WebConnect_SendResponseCode(405)
End case

Profiler_STOP(Current method name)
```

## Security Requirements
1. Never process protected actions when unauthorized.
2. Never trust URL or form values without validation.
3. Never allow POST processing without CSRF checks.
4. Never return sensitive details in error responses.


## Routing Requirements
1. Register new routes only in the approved startup routing methods.
2. Keep route paths stable and predictable.
3. Match route registration and handler naming conventions.
4. Prefer one handler per route responsibility.


## Error Handling
1. Use project-standard logging for expected and unexpected failures.
2. Return user-safe messages for UI flows.
3. Preserve technical error detail only in logs.


## Review Notes
1. Confirm exact CSRF validation method names used in this repository.
2. Confirm preferred response method for unsupported HTTP methods.
3. Confirm if all web handlers must be preemptive-capable.
